Présentation
Vous planifierez, coordonnerez et superviserez l'infrastructure et les services qui assurent la circulation efficace des biens et des personnes à destination, en provenance et au sein de l'Organisation, conformément aux règles et procédures de sécurité applicables. Vous appliquerez les meilleures pratiques et contribuerez à l'amélioration continue des processus logistiques et opérationnels, dans des domaines tels que la gestion des entrepôts et des stocks, la réception des marchandises, l'optimisation des processus, le suivi opérationnel basé sur les ERP, le suivi de l'ICP et la supervision des activités sous-traitées.
Fonctions

• Planifier, coordonner et optimiser la fourniture de services logistiques et d'entrepôts, en aidant les équipes opérationnelles, y compris l'équipe de l'entrepreneur, à assurer la qualité, la sécurité et l'efficacité des services logistiques.

• Agir en tant qu'interface entre les acteurs de la logistique, y compris les équipes d'entreposage, les achats, l'assistance technique et divers fournisseurs de services, maintenir une communication régulière avec les utilisateurs finaux du CERN et assurer un haut niveau de service à la clientèle.

• Surveiller le rendement opérationnel et contractuel, y compris les ICR, la facturation, les contrôles des paiements, les vérifications et les activités connexes.

• Surveiller le CERN Entreposer les activités de reconstitution en collaboration étroite avec l'équipe de référence du CERN et fournir un appui sur les questions et améliorations liées au PGI.

• Participer et diriger des projets liés à la logistique en collaboration avec des intervenants internes et externes.

Baccalauréat ou expérience équivalente pertinente dans le domaine de la chaîne d'approvisionnement et de la gestion logistique ou un domaine connexe.
La ceinture verte LEAN ou la certification équivalente est une valeur ajoutée au profil.
Expérience :

• Expérience approfondie de la gestion de la chaîne d'approvisionnement ou d'un domaine connexe, y compris la coordination des opérations quotidiennes de la chaîne d'approvisionnement et des projets connexes et le suivi des activités des entrepreneurs.

• Expérience de l'amélioration continue dans le domaine de la chaîne logistique et de l'élaboration de normes et de documents relatifs aux opérations.

• Compétence dans l'utilisation des systèmes ERP/MRP, dépannage opérationnel et outils MS Office.
Compétences techniques:

• Gestion des entrepôts et des stocks.

• Réception et distribution des biens.

• Service clientèle.

• Spécification et suivi des aspects techniques d'un contrat.

• Démontrer la responsabilité : travailler consciencieusement et de manière fiable; tenir les promesses.

• Établir des relations : comprendre comment les différences individuelles apportent une valeur ajoutée à l'Organisation; promouvoir les complémentarités.

• Démontrer la flexibilité : être prêt à travailler simultanément sur différents projets.

• Résoudre les problèmes : identifier, définir et évaluer les problèmes, prendre des mesures pour y remédier.

• Gérer soi : travailler bien de manière autonome; entreprendre des activités et des tâches sans enclencher.

Parlé et écrit à la fois anglais et français.

Flexibilité de l'emploi : hybride
Cette position implique:

Domaine de travail: Logistique & Transports

• Un salaire compétitif (sans impôt), en hausse en fonction de vos années d'expérience pertinente.

• Allocations mensuelles pour la famille, l'enfant et l'enfant selon votre situation personnelle.

• Un forfait de réinstallation (subvention d'installation, déménagement, frais de déplacement) selon votre situation personnelle.

Au CERN, l'Organisation européenne pour la recherche nucléaire, nous repoussons les frontières de la science et de la technologie. Ensemble, nous favorisons un environnement où l'innovation et la collaboration prospèrent.
Chaque jour, nous faisons face à de nouveaux défis passionnants et à de nouvelles occasions de contribuer à la recherche de pointe qui façonne notre compréhension de l'univers. Nous relevons ces défis grâce aux diverses perspectives au sein de nos équipes, en veillant à ce que chaque contribution soit valorisée et à ce que notre sens commun de l'inclusion et de l'objectif soit déterminé. La diversité est une valeur fondamentale du CERN depuis sa fondation, et elle demeure au cœur de notre mission et de notre succès continu.
Si vous êtes prêt à faire partie d'une communauté dynamique et inclusive qui repousse les limites du savoir, le CERN est l'endroit où votre curiosité et vos compétences peuvent prospérer. Faites partie de notre mission de découvrir ce qui est au cœur de l'univers ! S'il vous plaît !

jobs.description:
Are you a creative communicator who enjoys turning complexity into stories people can understand and relate to? Are you interested in people, transformation and the role communication can play in bringing the two together?
 Join CERN's Human Capital Management (HCM) project and help us communicate one of the Organization's major transformations. HCM will reshape the HR systems and processes supporting people throughout their working lives at CERN, creating a more connected experience from recruitment to departure.
 As part of the HCM Change and Adoption team, you will help bring this transformation closer to CERN's diverse community. You will contribute to shaping our communications approach and turn it into clear, engaging, audience-focused communications that help people understand what is changing, why it matters, and what it means for them.
 Your responsibilities:

• Translate the HCM project's communication strategy into concrete communication activities.

• Plan and deliver communications around the project milestones, managing multiple deliverables and deadlines autonomously.

• Turn complex information into clear and engaging messages for different audiences, working closely with experts and stakeholders.

• Create content across a broad range of channels and formats, including posts, emails, webpages, presentations, one-pagers, communication toolkits, videos and other multimedia content.

• Manage HCM communication channels and editorial planning.

• Contribute to wider change and adoption activities such as surveys and learning materials.
 Your profile

• Professional experience in communications, ideally in organisational change, large-scale transformation project, or another complex multistakeholder environment.

• Demonstrated ability translating complex information into clear and engaging content for different audiences.

• Experience managing communication activities and an editorial calendar against multiple deadlines and milestones.

• Experience with common content creation, web, presentation and visual communication tools; experience creating or coordinating video/multimedia content would be an advantage.

• Proactive, collaborative and eager to learn in a dynamic project environment.
 Skills:

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English; knowledge of French an advantage.

• Ability to communicate with clarity, creativity and attention to detail.

• Strong organisation skills and ability to manage multiple activities and deadlines.

• Collaborative and confident working with people from different backgrounds and areas of expertise.

• Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
 Eligibility criteria:

• You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State .

• You have a professional background in Communications, Marketing or related (or a related field) and have either:
• a Master's degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience;

• or a PhD with no more than 3 years of post-graduation professional experience.

• You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

Job closing date: 15.11.2026 at 23:59 CET.
 Contract duration: 24 months, with a possible extension up to 36 months maximum.
 Working hours: 40 hours per week
 Job flexibility: Hybrid
 Target start date: 01-January-2027
 Job reference: HR-PXE-2026-164-GRAP
 Field of work: Communication & Stakeholder Engagement
 Benchmark job: 5B0170 - Communications/Public Relations/External Relations Support Officer

Global Benefits

• A monthly net stipend of either 6372 or 7004 Swiss Francs per month depending on your degree.

• 30 days of paid leave per year plus 2 weeks annual closure.

• Coverage by CERN’s comprehensive health insurance scheme (for yourself, your spouse and children), and membership of the CERN Pension Fund.

• Family, child and infant monthly allowances depending on your individual circumstances.

• A relocation package (installation grant and travel expenses) depending on your individual circumstances.

• Possibility to extend your contract up to 36 months.

• On-the-job and formal training including language classes.

descriptionByLocale.it:
Sei un comunicatore creativo che gode di trasformare la complessità in storie con cui le persone possono capire e relazionarsi? Siete interessati alle persone, alla trasformazione e alla comunicazione di ruolo che possono svolgere nel riunire i due?
Unisciti al progetto Human Capital Management (HCM) del CERN e aiutaci a comunicare una delle principali trasformazioni dell'Organizzazione. HCM rimodellerà i sistemi e i processi HR supportando le persone durante la loro vita lavorativa al CERN, creando un'esperienza più connessa dal reclutamento alla partenza.
Nell'ambito del team HCM Change and Adoption, vi aiuterà a avvicinare questa trasformazione alla comunità diversificata del CERN. Contribuirai a modellare il nostro approccio di comunicazione e a trasformarlo in comunicazioni chiare, coinvolgenti e focalizzate sul pubblico che aiutano le persone a capire cosa sta cambiando, perché conta e cosa significa per loro.
Le tue responsabilità:

• Traduci la strategia di comunicazione del progetto HCM in attività di comunicazione concreta.

• Pianifica e rilascia comunicazioni intorno alle pietre miliari del progetto, gestendo più consegnabili e scadenze in modo autonomo.

• Trasformare le informazioni complesse in messaggi chiari e coinvolgenti per il pubblico diverso, lavorando a stretto contatto con esperti e stakeholder.

• Crea contenuti attraverso una vasta gamma di canali e formati, tra cui post, e-mail, pagine web, presentazioni, one-pagers, toolkit di comunicazione, video e altri contenuti multimediali.

• Gestisci canali di comunicazione HCM e pianificazione editoriale.

• Contribuisci ad attività di cambiamento e adozione più ampie, quali sondaggi e materiali di apprendimento.
Il tuo profilo

• Esperienza professionale nelle comunicazioni, idealmente in cambiamento organizzativo, progetto di trasformazione su larga scala, o un altro ambiente multistakeholder complesso.

• Capacità dimostrata di tradurre informazioni complesse in contenuti chiari e coinvolgenti per il pubblico diverso.

• Esperienza di gestione delle attività di comunicazione e un calendario editoriale contro più scadenze e tappe.

• Esperienza con strumenti comuni di creazione di contenuti, web, presentazione e comunicazione visiva; la creazione o il coordinamento di contenuti video/multimedia sarebbe un vantaggio.

• Proattivo, collaborativo e desideroso di imparare in un ambiente di progetto dinamico.
Competenze:

• Eccellente capacità di comunicazione scritta e verbale in inglese; conoscenza del francese un vantaggio.

• Capacità di comunicare con chiarezza, creatività e attenzione ai dettagli.

• Forte capacità organizzativa e capacità di gestire più attività e scadenze.

• Lavoro collaborativo e fiducioso con persone di diversa provenienza e aree di competenza.

• Parlato e scritto inglese, con un impegno per imparare il francese.
Criteri di ammissibilità:

• Sei un cittadino di uno Stato membro del CERN o di uno Stato membro associato .

• Hai uno sfondo professionale in Comunicazioni, Marketing o relativi (o un campo correlato) e hanno o:
• un Master con 2 a 6 anni di esperienza professionale post-graduazione;

• o un dottorato con non più di 3 anni di esperienza professionale post-graduazione.

• Non hai mai avuto un contratto di laurea o di socio del CERN.

Data di chiusura del lavoro: 15.11.2026 alle 23:59 CET.
Durata del contratto: 24 mesi, con una possibile estensione fino a 36 mesi massimo.
Orario di lavoro: 40 ore settimanali
Flessibilità del lavoro: ibrido
Data di inizio obiettivo: 01-gennaio-2027
Riferimento del lavoro: HR-PXE-2026-164-GRAP
Campo di lavoro: Comunicazione e coinvolgimento degli stakeholder
Benchmark job: 5B0170 - Comunicazioni/Relazioni Pubbliche/Relazioni Esterne

Vantaggi globali

• Una spesa netta mensile di 6372 o 7004 franchi svizzeri al mese a seconda della laurea.

• 30 giorni di congedo retribuito all'anno più 2 settimane di chiusura annuale.

• Copertura dell’assicurazione sanitaria completa del CERN (per te, il tuo coniuge e i tuoi figli) e dell’iscrizione al CERN Pension Fund.

• Indennità mensili di famiglia, bambino e bambino a seconda delle circostanze individuali.

• Un pacchetto di trasferimento (concessione di installazione e spese di viaggio) a seconda delle vostre circostanze individuali.

• Possibilità di estendere il contratto fino a 36 mesi.

• On-the-job e formazione formale, comprese le lezioni di lingua.
Panoramica del CERN - Scopri un mondo in cui l'impossibile è reso possibile!
Al CERN, l'Organizzazione europea per la ricerca nucleare, stiamo spingendo le frontiere della scienza e della tecnologia. Il nostro lavoro innovativo riunisce non solo i fisici, ma anche una vasta gamma di professionisti provenienti da settori ingegneristici, tecnici, scientifici e amministrativi. Insieme, promuoviamo un ambiente in cui l'innovazione e la collaborazione prosperano.
Ogni giorno, affrontiamo nuove sfide e opportunità entusiasmanti per contribuire alla ricerca all'avanguardia che plasma la nostra comprensione dell'universo. Incontriamo queste sfide attraverso le diverse prospettive all'interno dei nostri team, assicurando che ogni contributo sia valutato e guida il nostro senso condiviso di inclusione e scopo. La diversità è un valore fondamentale del CERN fin dalla sua fondazione, e rimane centrale per la nostra missione e il successo continuo.
Se siete pronti a far parte di una comunità dinamica e inclusiva che spinge i confini della conoscenza, il CERN è il luogo in cui la vostra curiosità e abilità possono prosperare. Fate parte della nostra missione per scoprire cosa sta nel cuore dell'universo! Partita!
Maggiori informazioni su di noi, qui: careers.cern

jobs.description:
We are offering a position in the Physics Software Engineering section of the Computing for Experiments group in the CERN IT department (IT-CE-PSE) on Performance Software Engineering in the realm of high energy physics data simulation.
 The work on this post will be carried out in the context of the NextGen project, a collaboration between the LHC experiments and the CERN Research and Computing Departments. NextGen explores the use and impact of high-performance computing architectures in data simulation and data processing for the LHC experiments with a focus on the upcoming High Luminosity (HL-LHC) data taking phase at the CERN Large Hadron Collider.
 The simulation of particle collisions is one of the main consumers of computing resources for LHC experiments. Given the expected increase in the required statistics, accuracy and complexity for future simulation, and to stay within the forecasted computing budget, the throughput of simulation software packages needs to increase substantially.
 The successful candidate will join a team of software engineers and physicists that addresses this challenge. Together, you will speed up software packages for Monte Carlo (MC) event generation with a focus on the Madgraph event generator suite. Current and future tasks tackled by the team are at the intersection of theoretical/computational physics and computer science. In order to profit from the latest computing hardware, adaptations or re-engineering of software in aspects such as data structures, parallelisation of the workflow or task scheduling are needed. This work is guided by the requirements of experimental analyses and takes into account the latest developments in theoretical predictions.
 In case of interest, training on data science, programming languages, software engineering concepts and computing architectures is available and can be provided via various training programs.
 Your responsibilities:

• Analyse and profile existing simulation code bases and develop strategies for improving their throughput.

• Implement latest software engineering concepts, leveraging on compute accelerators such as GPUs, modern CPU architectures and heterogeneous compute platforms.

• Interact and collaborate with experts in the theory, experimental physics and software engineering communities at CERN and world-wide.

• Supervise students on software development tasks and projects.
 Your profile:

• Preferably a PhD in Theoretical or Particle Physics or Master's Degree with equivalent work experience with a strong background in numerical simulation.

• Proficiency in working with computing hardware accelerators and modern computing architectures, including heterogeneous compute platforms.

• A proven track record in performance software engineering for simulation applications in C++ and GPU programming languages such as CUDA or HIP.

• Knowledge of state of the art profiling tools for heterogeneous computing architectures.

• Experience with the Madgraph event generator software as a developer or user is highly valued.
 Skills:

• Proficiency in modern C++ (up to C++23), GPU programming with CUDA and HIP, and Python for scripting, analysis and tooling is essential.

• Knowledge of hard scattering processes and the perturbative order of their matrix element calculations in Monte Carlo event generators is strongly desirable.

• Familiarity with Fortran is an advantage.

• Fluent in English.

• Spoken and written English or French, with a commitment to learn the basics of the other language.
 Eligibility criteria:

• You have a professional background in Theoretical or Particle Physics (or a related field) and have either:
• a Master's Degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience;

• or a PhD with no more than 3 years of post-graduation professional experience.

• You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

 Contract duration: 24 months, with a possible extension up to 36 months maximum.
 Working hours: 40 hours per week

descriptionByLocale.it:
Stiamo offrendo una posizione nella sezione Ingegneria del Software di Fisica del gruppo Computing for Experiments nel dipartimento IT CERN (IT-CE-PSE) su Performance Software Engineering nel regno della simulazione di dati di fisica ad alta energia.
Il lavoro su questo post sarà svolto nel contesto del progetto NextGen, una collaborazione tra gli esperimenti LHC e i Dipartimenti di Ricerca e Computing del CERN. NextGen esplora l'uso e l'impatto di architetture di calcolo ad alte prestazioni nella simulazione dei dati e nell'elaborazione dei dati per gli esperimenti LHC con un focus sui prossimi dati High Luminosity (HL-LHC) che prendono fase al CERN Large Hadron Collider.
La simulazione di collisioni di particelle è uno dei principali consumatori di risorse di calcolo per gli esperimenti LHC. Data l'aumento previsto delle statistiche richieste, l'accuratezza e la complessità per la simulazione futura, e per rimanere all'interno del bilancio di calcolo previsto, il throughput dei pacchetti software di simulazione deve aumentare notevolmente.
Il candidato di successo si unirà a un team di ingegneri e fisici software che affronta questa sfida. Insieme, velocizzerai i pacchetti software per la generazione di eventi Monte Carlo (MC) con un focus sulla suite generatore di eventi Madgraph. I compiti attuali e futuri affrontati dal team sono all'incrocio tra fisica teorica/computazionale e scienza informatica. Al fine di trarre profitto dall'hardware di calcolo più recente, sono necessari adattamenti o riingegneria del software in aspetti come le strutture di dati, la parallelizzazione del flusso di lavoro o la pianificazione delle attività. Questo lavoro è guidato dai requisiti delle analisi sperimentali e tiene conto degli ultimi sviluppi delle previsioni teoriche.
In caso di interesse, la formazione sulla scienza dei dati, linguaggi di programmazione, concetti di ingegneria del software e architetture di calcolo è disponibile e può essere fornito tramite vari programmi di formazione.
Le tue responsabilità:

• Analizzare e profilare le basi di codice di simulazione esistenti e sviluppare strategie per migliorare il loro throughput.

• Implementare i più recenti concetti di ingegneria del software, sfruttando gli acceleratori di calcolo come GPU, moderne architetture della CPU e piattaforme di calcolo eterogenee.

• Interagire e collaborare con esperti nelle comunità di teoria, fisica sperimentale e ingegneria software del CERN e mondiale.

• Superare gli studenti sulle attività di sviluppo software e progetti.
Il tuo profilo:

• Preferibilmente un dottorato in Fisica Teorica o Particella o Laurea Magistrale con esperienza lavorativa equivalente con un forte background in simulazione numerica.

• La competenza nel lavorare con gli acceleratori hardware di calcolo e le moderne architetture di calcolo, comprese le piattaforme di calcolo eterogenee.

• Un collaudato track record nell'ingegneria del software di performance per applicazioni di simulazione in linguaggi di programmazione C++ e GPU come CUDA o HIP.

• Conoscenza degli strumenti di profilazione dell'arte per architetture di calcolo eterogenee.

• L'esperienza con il software del generatore di eventi Madgraph come sviluppatore o utente è altamente apprezzata.
Competenze:

• La competenza nel C++ moderno (fino a C++23), la programmazione GPU con CUDA e HIP, e Python per la scrittura, l'analisi e l'attrezzo è essenziale.

• La conoscenza dei processi di spargimento duro e l'ordine perturbativo dei calcoli degli elementi di matrice nei generatori di eventi di Monte Carlo è fortemente auspicabile.

• La familiarità con Fortran è un vantaggio.

• Fluente in inglese.

• Parlato e scritto inglese o francese, con l'impegno di imparare le basi dell'altra lingua.
Criteri di ammissibilità:

• Hai uno sfondo professionale in Fisica Teoretica o Particella (o un campo correlato) e hanno o:
• un Master con 2 a 6 anni di esperienza professionale post-graduazione;

• o un dottorato con non più di 3 anni di esperienza professionale post-graduazione.

• Non hai mai avuto un contratto di laurea o di socio del CERN.

Data di chiusura del lavoro: 13.11.2026 alle 23:59 CET.
Durata del contratto: 24 mesi, con una possibile estensione fino a 36 mesi massimo.
Orario di lavoro: 40 ore settimanali
Flessibilità del lavoro: ibrido
Data di inizio obiettivo: 01-gennaio-2027
Questa posizione comporta:

• In piedi, quando richiesto dalle esigenze dell'Organizzazione.

• Lavorare durante le notti, la domenica e le vacanze ufficiali, quando richiesto dalle esigenze dell'Organizzazione.
Riferimento del lavoro: IT-CE-PSE-2026-167-GRAP
Campo di lavoro: Tecnologie dell'informazione
Lavoro Benchmark: 200020 - Ingegnere di calcolo

Vantaggi globali

• Una spesa netta mensile di 6372 o 7004 franchi svizzeri al mese a seconda della laurea.

• 30 giorni di congedo retribuito all'anno più 2 settimane di chiusura annuale.

• Copertura dell’assicurazione sanitaria completa del CERN (per te, il tuo coniuge e i tuoi figli) e dell’iscrizione al CERN Pension Fund.

• Indennità mensili di famiglia, bambino e bambino a seconda delle circostanze individuali.

• Un pacchetto di trasferimento (concessione di installazione e spese di viaggio) a seconda delle vostre circostanze individuali.

• Possibilità di estendere il contratto fino a 36 mesi.

• On-the-job e formazione formale, comprese le lezioni di lingua.
Panoramica del CERN - Scopri un mondo in cui l'impossibile è reso possibile!
Al CERN, l'Organizzazione europea per la ricerca nucleare, stiamo spingendo le frontiere della scienza e della tecnologia. Il nostro lavoro innovativo riunisce non solo i fisici, ma anche una vasta gamma di professionisti provenienti da settori ingegneristici, tecnici, scientifici e amministrativi. Insieme, promuoviamo un ambiente in cui l'innovazione e la collaborazione prosperano.
Ogni giorno, affrontiamo nuove sfide e opportunità entusiasmanti per contribuire alla ricerca all'avanguardia che plasma la nostra comprensione dell'universo. Incontriamo queste sfide attraverso le diverse prospettive all'interno dei nostri team, assicurando che ogni contributo sia valutato e guida il nostro senso condiviso di inclusione e scopo. La diversità è un valore fondamentale del CERN fin dalla sua fondazione, e rimane centrale per la nostra missione e il successo continuo.
Se siete pronti a far parte di una comunità dinamica e inclusiva che spinge i confini della conoscenza, il CERN è il luogo in cui la vostra curiosità e abilità possono prosperare. Fate parte della nostra missione per scoprire cosa sta nel cuore dell'universo! Partita!

Wir bieten eine Position im Bereich Physics Software Engineering der Gruppe Computing for Experiments in der CERN IT-Abteilung (IT-CE-PSE) zum Thema Performance Software Engineering im Bereich der Hochenergiephysik-Datensimulation an.
Die Arbeit an diesem Beitrag wird im Rahmen des NextGen-Projekts durchgeführt, einer Zusammenarbeit zwischen den LHC-Experimenten und den CERN-Forschungs- und Computerabteilungen. NextGen untersucht den Einsatz und die Auswirkungen von Hochleistungs-Computing-Architekturen in der Datensimulation und Datenverarbeitung für die LHC-Experimente mit Schwerpunkt auf der bevorstehenden High Luminosity (HL-LHC)-Datenphase am CERN Large Hadron Collider.
Die Simulation von Teilchenkollisionen ist einer der Hauptverbraucher von Rechenressourcen für LHC-Experimente. Angesichts der erwarteten Zunahme der erforderlichen Statistiken, Genauigkeit und Komplexität für zukünftige Simulationen und um im Rahmen des prognostizierten Rechenbudgets zu bleiben, muss der Durchsatz von Simulationssoftwarepaketen erheblich erhöht werden.
Der erfolgreiche Kandidat wird sich einem Team von Softwareingenieuren und Physikern anschließen, das sich dieser Herausforderung stellt. Gemeinsam beschleunigen Sie Softwarepakete für die Monte Carlo (MC) Event Generation mit Schwerpunkt auf der Madgraph Event Generator Suite. Aktuelle und zukünftige Aufgaben, die das Team in Angriff nimmt, befinden sich an der Schnittstelle zwischen theoretischer/rechnerischer Physik und Informatik. Um von der neuesten Computerhardware zu profitieren, sind Anpassungen oder Re-Engineering von Software in Aspekten wie Datenstrukturen, Parallelisierung des Workflows oder Aufgabenplanung erforderlich. Diese Arbeit orientiert sich an den Anforderungen experimenteller Analysen und berücksichtigt die neuesten Entwicklungen bei theoretischen Vorhersagen.
Bei Interesse stehen Schulungen zu Data Science, Programmiersprachen, Software Engineering Konzepten und Rechenarchitekturen zur Verfügung und können über verschiedene Schulungsprogramme bereitgestellt werden.
Ihre Aufgaben:

• Analyse und Profilierung bestehender Simulationscodebasen und Entwicklung von Strategien zur Verbesserung ihres Durchsatzes.

• Implementieren Sie neueste Software-Engineering-Konzepte und nutzen Sie Rechenbeschleuniger wie GPUs, moderne CPU-Architekturen und heterogene Rechenplattformen.

• Interagieren und arbeiten Sie mit Experten aus den Bereichen Theorie, experimentelle Physik und Softwareentwicklung am CERN und weltweit zusammen.

• Beaufsichtigen Sie Studenten bei Softwareentwicklungsaufgaben und -projekten.
Ihr Profil:

• Vorzugsweise ein PhD in Theoretische oder Teilchenphysik oder Master-Abschluss mit gleichwertiger Berufserfahrung mit einem starken Hintergrund in der numerischen Simulation.

• Kenntnisse in der Arbeit mit Hardwarebeschleunigern und modernen Computerarchitekturen, einschließlich heterogener Rechenplattformen.

• Eine nachgewiesene Erfolgsbilanz im Bereich Performance Software Engineering für Simulationsanwendungen in C++ und GPU-Programmiersprachen wie CUDA oder HIP.

• Kenntnis des Stands der Technik Profiling-Tools für heterogene Computerarchitekturen.

• Erfahrung mit der Madgraph Event Generator Software als Entwickler oder Benutzer wird sehr geschätzt.
Fähigkeiten:

• Kenntnisse in modernen C++ (bis C++23), GPU-Programmierung mit CUDA und HIP sowie Python für Skripting, Analyse und Tooling sind unerlässlich.

• Die Kenntnis von harten Streuprozessen und der störenden Ordnung ihrer Matrixelementberechnungen in Monte-Carlo-Ereignisgeneratoren ist dringend wünschenswert.

• Die Vertrautheit mit Fortran ist von Vorteil.

• fließend in Englisch.

Nous vous proposons un poste dans la section Ingénierie des logiciels de physique du groupe Computing for Experiments du département IT du CERN (IT-CE-PSE) sur l'ingénierie des logiciels de performance dans le domaine de la simulation de données de physique de haute énergie.
Les travaux sur ce poste seront réalisés dans le cadre du projet NextGen, une collaboration entre les expériences LHC et les départements de recherche et de calcul du CERN. NextGen explore l'utilisation et l'impact des architectures informatiques de haute performance dans la simulation et le traitement des données pour les expériences LHC en mettant l'accent sur la prochaine phase de prise de données High Luminosity (HL-LHC) au CERN Large Hadron Collider.
La simulation des collisions de particules est l'un des principaux consommateurs de ressources informatiques pour les expériences de LHC. Compte tenu de l'augmentation prévue des statistiques, de l'exactitude et de la complexité des simulations futures, et pour rester dans les limites du budget de calcul prévu, le débit des progiciels de simulation doit augmenter considérablement.
La candidate reçue se joindra à une équipe d'ingénieurs en logiciels et de physiciens qui relèvera ce défi. Ensemble, vous allez accélérer les paquets logiciels pour la génération d'événements Monte Carlo (MC) en mettant l'accent sur la suite de générateurs d'événements Madgraph. Les tâches actuelles et futures de l'équipe sont à l'intersection de la physique théorique/computationnelle et de l'informatique. Afin de bénéficier du matériel informatique le plus récent, il est nécessaire d'adapter ou de réorganiser les logiciels dans des aspects tels que les structures de données, la parallélisation du flux de travail ou la planification des tâches. Ce travail est guidé par les exigences des analyses expérimentales et prend en compte les derniers développements des prévisions théoriques.
En cas d'intérêt, une formation sur la science des données, les langages de programmation, les concepts d'ingénierie logicielle et les architectures informatiques est disponible et peut être fournie par le biais de divers programmes de formation.
Vos responsabilités :

• Analyser et profiler les bases de codes de simulation existantes et élaborer des stratégies pour améliorer leur débit.

• Mettre en œuvre les concepts d'ingénierie logicielle les plus récents, en tirant parti des accélérateurs de calcul tels que les GPU, les architectures CPU modernes et les plates-formes de calcul hétérogènes.

• Interagir et collaborer avec des experts en théorie, en physique expérimentale et en génie logiciel au CERN et dans le monde entier.

• Superviser les étudiants sur les tâches et les projets de développement logiciel.
Votre profil:

• De préférence un doctorat en physique théorique ou par particules ou une maîtrise avec une expérience de travail équivalente avec une solide expérience en simulation numérique.

• Compétence dans le travail avec les accélérateurs de matériel informatique et les architectures informatiques modernes, y compris les plates-formes informatiques hétérogènes.

• Une expérience éprouvée en ingénierie de logiciels de performance pour des applications de simulation en langages de programmation C++ et GPU tels que CUDA ou HIP.

• Connaissance des outils de profilage de pointe pour les architectures informatiques hétérogènes.

• L'expérience avec le logiciel de générateur d'événements Madgraph en tant que développeur ou utilisateur est très appréciée.
Compétences :

• La compétence en C++ moderne (jusqu'à C++23), la programmation GPU avec CUDA et HIP et Python pour le script, l'analyse et l'outillage est essentielle.

• La connaissance des processus de diffusion dure et l'ordre perturbatif de leurs calculs d'éléments de matrice dans les générateurs d'événements Monte Carlo est fortement souhaitable.

• La familiarité avec Fortran est un avantage.

• En anglais.

• Parlé et écrit anglais ou français, avec un engagement à apprendre les bases de l'autre langue.
Critères d'éligibilité:

• Vous avez une formation professionnelle en physique théorique ou par particules (ou dans un domaine connexe) et avez :
• une maîtrise de 2 à 6 ans d'expérience professionnelle après l'obtention du diplôme;

• ou d'un doctorat d'au plus trois ans d'expérience professionnelle après l'obtention du diplôme.

• Vous n'avez jamais eu de CERN ni de contrat d'études supérieures.

titleByLocale.fr: Physicien de la reconstruction des événements (EP-FCC-2026-166-GRAP)

jobs.description:
The next generation of experiments, the HL-LHC upgrade of CMS and the Future Circular Collider, needs event reconstruction that is fast, accurate and portable across CPUs and GPUs. Every reconstruction algorithm and every machine-learning model is trained and judged against the simulation truth. Today that truth is stored in static, detector-specific objects. Each object is pre-grouped for one purpose, it cannot be navigated, and it separates calorimeter truth from tracker truth.
 CERN has built a prototype that replaces them. It is one navigable, event-level graph of the generator and simulation history, with calorimeter and tracker hit indices on top. Reconstruction code then reasons in terms of stable physics abstractions: particles, vertices, decay branches and hits.
 You will make this the truth model of the future. You will generalise the prototype into an experiment-independent library, you will bring it into the FCC software stack, and you will use it to build the next reconstruction: graph algorithms and modern machine learning for clustering, particle flow and particle identification, and reliable matching between reconstructed objects and truth. You will join the EP-FCC group, and you will work on both CMS and FCC-ee.
 Your responsibilities:

• Generalise the CMS MC-truth graph into a detector-independent and experiment-independent library. Separate the graph data model, the navigation API and the hit index from the experiment data-format bindings.

• Develop the bindings. Keep the CMSSW binding working, and add a binding for the FCC stack (Key4hep, EDM4hep, Gaudi), so that both experiments build the same graph from their own simulation output.

• Extend the data model. Add multi-surface boundary crossings, sparse association storage, and a reduced hit-index layout. Handle pileup consistently.

• Develop the reconstruction-to-truth association. Extend the adaptive branch associator, which selects the truth level that best matches a reconstructed object, and validate it on merged topologies such as converted photons, bremsstrahlung and early hadronic interactions.

• Define what is reconstructible. Derive it from the truth graph and the detector description, using cell granularity, energy and time resolution, readout thresholds and two-object separation.

• Apply portable graph algorithms and advanced machine learning, for example graph neural networks and transformers, to reconstruction tasks in CMS (HGCAL and TICL) and in FCC detectors: clustering, linking, particle flow and particle identification.

• Build the training datasets and the labels from the truth graph. Define the metrics, calibrate the model outputs, and check the model before it feeds reconstruction.

• Contribute the code to the official repositories of CMS and of the FCC software stack, with unit tests, documentation and code review.

• Present the results in CMS and FCC meetings, in software forums and in publications.

• This role includes team supervision responsibilities.
 Your profile:

• A Master's Degree or a PhD in Physics, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics or a related field.

• Demonstrated experience with modern C++ in a large, shared and peer-reviewed codebase, for example CMSSW, Gaudi or Key4hep.

• Demonstrated experience with time-aware event reconstruction and detector simulation in a high-energy physics experiment.

• Demonstrated experience with heterogeneous and portable computing, for example Alpaka, SYCL, CUDA or HIP.

• Experience with Python and with at least one machine-learning framework, preferably PyTorch.

• Experience with graph and clustering algorithms.

• Experience with git, code review and continuous integration.
 Skills:

• C++20.

• Clustering, event reconstruction.

• Detector simulation.

• Particle flow.

• CMSSW,Key4hep.

• Heterogeneous computing.

• Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
 Eligibility criteria:

• You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State .

• You have a professional background in Physics (or a related field) and have either:
• a Master's degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience;

• or a PhD with no more than 3 years of post-graduation professional experience.

• You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

descriptionByLocale.it:
La prossima generazione di esperimenti, l'aggiornamento HL-LHC di CMS e il Future Circular Collider, ha bisogno di ricostruzione di eventi che è veloce, preciso e portatile attraverso CPU e GPU. Ogni algoritmo di ricostruzione e ogni modello di apprendimento automatico è addestrato e giudicato contro la verità di simulazione. Oggi quella verità è memorizzata in oggetti statici e specifici per rivelatori. Ogni oggetto è pre-gruppo per uno scopo, non può essere navigato, e separa la verità calorimetrica dalla verità tracker.
Il CERN ha costruito un prototipo che li sostituisce. Si tratta di un grafico navigabile, a livello di eventi della storia del generatore e della simulazione, con calorimetro e indici di successo del tracker in cima. Codice di ricostruzione quindi motivi in termini di astrazioni fisiche stabili: particelle, vertici, rami di decadimento e colpi.
Renderai questo il modello di verità del futuro. Generalizzerai il prototipo in una libreria indipendente dall'esperimento, lo porterai nello stack software FCC, e lo userai per costruire la prossima ricostruzione: algoritmi di grafo e apprendimento moderno della macchina per clustering, flusso di particelle e identificazione delle particelle, e un'affidabile corrispondenza tra oggetti ricostruiti e verità. Ti unirai al gruppo EP-FCC e lavorerai sia su CMS che su FCC-ee.
Le tue responsabilità:

• Generalizzare il grafico CMS MC-truth in una libreria indipendente e indipendente da esperimenti. Separare il modello di dati grafico, l'API di navigazione e l'indice di successo dai binding di data-format dell'esperimento.

• Sviluppare gli attacchi. Mantenere il lavoro di binding CMSSW e aggiungere un binding per lo stack FCC (Key4hep, EDM4hep, Gaudi), in modo che entrambi gli esperimenti costruiscano lo stesso grafico dalla propria uscita di simulazione.

• Estendere il modello di dati. Aggiunga i passaggi di confine multi-superficie, lo stoccaggio di associazione rada, e un layout di hit-index ridotto. Maniglia pileup costantemente.

• Sviluppare l'associazione ricostruzione-verità. Estendere l'associatore di ramo adattativo, che seleziona il livello di verità che meglio corrisponde a un oggetto ricostruito, e convalidarlo su topologie fuse come fotoni convertiti, bremsstrahlung e prime interazioni hadronic.

• Definire ciò che è ricostruibile. Deducilo dal grafico della verità e dalla descrizione del rivelatore, utilizzando granulosità cellulare, risoluzione dell'energia e del tempo, soglie di lettura e separazione a due oggetti.

• Applicare algoritmi di grafo portatili e l'apprendimento avanzato della macchina, ad esempio reti neurali di grafo e trasformatori, a compiti di ricostruzione in CMS (HGCAL e TICL) e nei rivelatori FCC: clustering, collegamento, flusso di particelle e identificazione delle particelle.

• Costruire i dataset di formazione e le etichette dal grafico della verità. Definire le metriche, calibrare le uscite del modello e controllare il modello prima di alimentare la ricostruzione.

• Contribuisci il codice ai repository ufficiali di CMS e dello stack software FCC, con test di unità, documentazione e revisione del codice.

• Presentare i risultati nelle riunioni CMS e FCC, nei forum software e nelle pubblicazioni.

• Questo ruolo include responsabilità di supervisione del team.
Il tuo profilo:

• Laurea Magistrale o dottorato in fisica, informatica, matematica applicata o un campo correlato.

• Esperienza dimostrata con C++ moderno in un grande, condiviso e peer-reviewed codebase, ad esempio CMSSW, Gaudi o Key4hep.

• Esperienza dimostrata con la ricostruzione di eventi e la simulazione di rivelatori nel tempo in un esperimento fisico ad alta energia.

• Esperienza dimostrata con calcolo eterogeneo e portatile, ad esempio Alpaka, SYCL, CUDA o HIP.

• Esperienza con Python e con almeno un quadro di apprendimento automatico, preferibilmente PyTorch.

• Esperienza con grafi e algoritmi di clustering.

• Esperienza con git, recensione del codice e integrazione continua.
Competenze:

• C++20.

• Clustering, ricostruzione eventi.

• Simulazione del rivelatore.

• Flusso di particelle.

• CMSSW,Key4hep.

• Informatica eterogenea.

• Parlato e scritto inglese, con un impegno per imparare il francese.
Criteri di ammissibilità:

• Sei un cittadino di uno Stato membro del CERN o di uno Stato membro associato .

• Hai uno sfondo professionale in Fisica (o un campo correlato) e hanno o:
• un Master con 2 a 6 anni di esperienza professionale post-graduazione;

• o un dottorato con non più di 3 anni di esperienza professionale post-graduazione.

• Non hai mai avuto un contratto di laurea o di socio del CERN.

You will generalise the prototype into an experiment-independent library, you will bring it into the FCC software stack, and you will use it to build the next reconstruction: graph algorithms and modern machine learning for clustering, particle flow and particle identification, and reliable matching between reconstructed objects and truth. You will join the EP-FCC group, and you will work on both CMS and FCC-ee.
Your responsibilities:

• Generalise the CMS MC-truth graph into a detector-independent and experiment-independent library. Separate the graph data model, the navigation API and the hit index from the experiment data-format bindings.

• Develop the bindings. Keep the CMSSW binding working, and add a binding for the FCC stack (Key4hep, EDM4hep, Gaudi), so that both experiments build the same graph from their own simulation output.

• Extend the data model. Add multi-surface boundary crossings, sparse association storage, and a reduced hit-index layout. Handle pileup consistently.

• Develop the reconstruction-to-truth association. Extend the adaptive branch associator, which selects the truth level that best matches a reconstructed object, and validate it on merged topologies such as converted photons, bremsstrahlung and early hadronic interactions.

• Define what is reconstructible. Derive it from the truth graph and the detector description, using cell granularity, energy and time resolution, readout thresholds and two-object separation.

• Apply portable graph algorithms and advanced machine learning, for example graph neural networks and transformers, to reconstruction tasks in CMS (HGCAL and TICL) and in FCC detectors: clustering, linking, particle flow and particle identification.

• Build the training datasets and the labels from the truth graph. Define the metrics, calibrate the model outputs, and check the model before it feeds reconstruction.

• Contribute the code to the official repositories of CMS and of the FCC software stack, with unit tests, documentation and code review.

• Present the results in CMS and FCC meetings, in software forums and in publications.

• This role includes team supervision responsibilities.
Your profile:

• Demonstrated experience with time-aware event reconstruction and detector simulation in a high-energy physics experiment.

• Demonstrated experience with heterogeneous and portable computing, for example Alpaka, SYCL, CUDA or HIP.

• Experience with Python and with at least one machine-learning framework, preferably PyTorch.

• Experience with graph and clustering algorithms.

• Experience with git, code review and continuous integration.

Die nächste Generation von Experimenten, das HL-LHC-Upgrade von CMS und der Future Circular Collider, erfordert eine schnelle, genaue und portable Ereignisrekonstruktion für CPUs und GPUs. Jeder Rekonstruktionsalgorithmus und jedes maschinelle Lernmodell wird trainiert und gegen die Simulationswahrheit beurteilt. Heute ist diese Wahrheit in statischen, detektorspezifischen Objekten gespeichert. Jedes Objekt ist für einen Zweck vorgruppiert, es kann nicht navigiert werden und trennt die Wahrheit des Kalorimeters von der Wahrheit des Trackers.
CERN hat einen Prototyp gebaut, der sie ersetzt. Es ist ein navigierbarer, ereignisbasierter Graph des Generators und der Simulationsgeschichte, mit Kalorimeter und Tracker-Hit-Indizes an der Spitze. Rekonstruktionscode Gründe dann in Bezug auf stabile Physikabstraktionen: Teilchen, Eckpunkte, Zerfallszweige und Treffer.
Ihr werdet dies zum Wahrheitsmodell der Zukunft machen. Sie verallgemeinern den Prototyp in eine experimentunabhängige Bibliothek, bringen ihn in den FCC-Software-Stack und verwenden ihn, um die nächste Rekonstruktion zu erstellen: Graphenalgorithmen und modernes maschinelles Lernen für Clustering, Partikelfluss und Partikelidentifikation und zuverlässige Übereinstimmung zwischen rekonstruierten Objekten und Wahrheit. Sie werden der EP-FCC-Gruppe beitreten und sowohl an CMS als auch an FCC-ee arbeiten.
Ihre Aufgaben:

• Verallgemeinern Sie den CMS-MC-Wahrheitsgraphen in eine detektorunabhängige und experimentunabhängige Bibliothek. Trennen Sie das Graphendatenmodell, die Navigations-API und den Trefferindex von den Bindungen im Experimentdatenformat.

• Die Bindungen entwickeln. Halten Sie die CMSSW-Bindung am Laufen und fügen Sie eine Bindung für den FCC-Stack (Key4hep, EDM4hep, Gaudi) hinzu, so dass beide Experimente den gleichen Graphen aus ihrer eigenen Simulationsausgabe erstellen.

• Erweitern Sie das Datenmodell. Fügen Sie mehrflächige Grenzüberschreitungen, Speicher für spärliche Assoziationen und ein reduziertes Hit-Index-Layout hinzu. Behandeln Sie Stampup konsequent.

• Entwickeln Sie die Rekonstruktion-zu-Wahrheit-Assoziation. Erweitern Sie den adaptiven Zweig-Assoziator, der die Wahrheitsstufe auswählt, die am besten zu einem rekonstruierten Objekt passt, und validieren Sie ihn auf fusionierten Topologien wie konvertierten Photonen, Bremsstrahlung und frühen hadronischen Wechselwirkungen.

• Definieren Sie, was rekonstruierbar ist. Ableiten aus dem Wahrheitsgraphen und der Detektorbeschreibung unter Verwendung von Zellgranularität, Energie- und Zeitauflösung, Ausleseschwellen und Zwei-Objekt-Trennung.

• Tragbare Graphenalgorithmen und fortgeschrittenes maschinelles Lernen, z. B. neuronale Graphennetze und Transformatoren, auf Rekonstruktionsaufgaben in CMS (HGCAL und TICL) und in FCC-Detektoren: Clustering, Verknüpfung, Partikelfluss und Partikelidentifikation.

• Präsentieren Sie die Ergebnisse in CMS- und FCC-Meetings, in Softwareforen und in Publikationen.

La prochaine génération d'expériences, la mise à niveau HL-LHC de la CMS et du Future Circular Collider, a besoin de reconstruction d'événements qui est rapide, précise et portable à travers les CPU et les GPU. Chaque algorithme de reconstruction et chaque modèle d'apprentissage automatique est formé et jugé par rapport à la vérité de simulation. Aujourd'hui, cette vérité est stockée dans des objets statiques spécifiques aux détecteurs. Chaque objet est pré-groupé dans un but, il ne peut pas être navigué, et il sépare la vérité calorimétrique de la vérité tracker.
Le CERN a construit un prototype qui les remplace. Il s'agit d'un graphique de niveau événementiel navigable de l'historique du générateur et de la simulation, avec des indices de calorimètre et de traqueur en haut. Le code de reconstruction explique alors en termes d'abstractions physiques stables : particules, vertices, branches de décomposition et hits.
Vous en ferez le modèle de vérité du futur. Vous généraliserez le prototype dans une bibliothèque indépendante de l'expérience, vous l'apporterez dans la pile de logiciels FCC, et vous l'utiliserez pour construire la prochaine reconstruction : algorithmes graphiques et apprentissage machine moderne pour le regroupement, le flux de particules et l'identification des particules, et une correspondance fiable entre les objets reconstruits et la vérité. Vous rejoindrez le groupe EP-FCC, et vous travaillerez à la fois sur la SMC et sur FAC-ee.
Vos responsabilités :

• Généraliser le graphique MC-vérité CMS dans une bibliothèque indépendante du détecteur et indépendante de l'expérience. Séparer le modèle de données graphiques, l'API de navigation et l'index de frappe des liaisons de format de données expérimentales.

• Développer les fixations. Conservez la liaison CMSSW et ajoutez une liaison pour la pile FCC (Key4hep, EDM4hep, Gaudi) afin que les deux expériences construisent le même graphique à partir de leur propre sortie de simulation.

• Étendre le modèle de données. Ajouter des passages à niveau multi-surfaces, un stockage d'associations éparpillées et une disposition réduite de l'indice de succès. Poignée empilée régulièrement.

• Développer l'association reconstruction-vérité. Étendre l'associateur de branche adaptative, qui sélectionne le niveau de vérité qui correspond le mieux à un objet reconstruit, et le valider sur des topologies fusionnées telles que les photons convertis, bremsstrahlung et les interactions hadroniques précoces.

• Définir ce qui est reconstructible. Dérivez-le du graphique de vérité et de la description du détecteur, en utilisant la granularité cellulaire, la résolution de l'énergie et du temps, les seuils de lecture et la séparation de deux objets.

• Appliquer des algorithmes graphiques portatifs et un apprentissage machine avancé, par exemple des réseaux neuronaux et des transformateurs graphiques, aux tâches de reconstruction en CMS (HGCAL et TICL) et dans les détecteurs FAC : regroupement, liaison, flux de particules et identification des particules.

• Construire les ensembles de données de formation et les étiquettes à partir du graphique de vérité. Définissez les paramètres, étalonnez les sorties du modèle et vérifiez le modèle avant qu'il n'alimente la reconstruction.

• Contribuez le code aux dépôts officiels du CMS et de la pile de logiciels de FAC, avec des tests unitaires, de la documentation et un examen de code.

• Présenter les résultats des réunions de la SMC et de FAC, des forums logiciels et des publications.

• Ce rôle comprend les responsabilités de supervision de l'équipe.
Votre profil:

• Maîtrise ou doctorat en physique, informatique, mathématiques appliquées ou domaine connexe.

• Expérience démontrée avec le C++ moderne dans une base de code large, partagée et évaluée par les pairs, par exemple CMSSW, Gaudi ou Key4hep.

• Expérience démontrée avec la reconstruction d'événements dans le temps et la simulation de détecteurs dans une expérience de physique à haute énergie.

descriptionByLocale.en:
Introduction
Within CERN’s Finance and Administrative Processes Department (FAP), specifically the Accounting Services Group. We are looking for a dynamic person to join our General Accounting (GA) section and play an active role in the accounting of CERN’s tangible and intangible assets, as well as its inventories. You will also support broader financial reporting activities and exciting accounting projects. There will be a particular focus on Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE).
As an experienced Accountant, you will join a team of seven professionals and play a key role in all activities related to asset accounting.
Functions
You will:

• Coordinate regular register(s) updates and reviews of useful lives and residual values with other CERN stakeholders.

• Analyse CERN projects to identify new assets or consolidation/upgrade of existing assets.

• Perform accounting entries related to movements of assets, depreciation/amortisation, and impairment tests.

• Support the ongoing ERP transformation project touching the areas of asset accounting and financial accounts.

• Perform balance sheet account reconciliations, including a reconciliation of assets register(s) to financial accounts.

• Maintain policies, procedures, and controls to ensure efficient, accurate, and compliant asset accounting.

• Coordinate physical assets counts.

• Support external auditors queries.

• Support preparation of the Organization’s Financial Statements, including assets related notes and disclosures.

• Maintain strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders.

Master's degree or equivalent relevant experience in the field of Accounting, Finance or a related field.
Accounting certification, such as ACA, CA, CPA, etc.
Experience:

• Proven experience as a general accountant with a focus on asset accounting, such as Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE).

• Demonstrated experience with international accounting standards IFRS and/or IPSAS.

• Experience preferably acquired in a company handling large volumes of data or in an international organisation.
Technical competencies:

• Accounting control and analysis, book-keeping and book-closing.

• Financial reporting and analysis, handling large volumes of data.
Behavioural competencies:

• Achieving Results: having a structured and organised approach towards work; being able to set priorities and plan tasks with results in mind.

• Demonstrating Accountability: using openness and honesty to interact constructively with others.

• Solving Problems: assimilating large quantities of information, identifying key issues and formulating conclusions clearly and concisely.

• Demonstrating Flexibility: demonstrating a willingness to accept changing circumstances; supporting initiatives for change.

• Managing Self: working well autonomously; taking on activities and tasks without prompting.
Language skills:
Spoken and written English or French, with a commitment to learn the other language.

Eligibility and closing date:
Diversity has been an integral part of CERN's mission since its foundation and is an established value of the Organization. Employing a diverse workforce is central to our success. We welcome applications from all Member States and Associate Member States .
This vacancy will be filled as soon as possible, and applications should normally reach us no later than 24.11.2026 at 23:59 CET .
Employment Conditions
Contract type: Limited duration contract (5 years). Subject to certain conditions, holders of limited-duration contracts may apply for an indefinite position.
Working Hours: 40 hours per week
Job Flexibility: Hybrid
Job grade: 6-7
Job reference: FAP-ACC-GA-2026-214-LD
Field of work: Finance, Control & Audit
Benchmark Job Title: Financial Professional

Global Benefits

• A competitive salary (tax free), increasing in line with your years of relevant experience.

• 30 days of paid leave per year plus 2 weeks annual closure.

• Coverage by CERN’s comprehensive health insurance scheme (for yourself, your spouse and children), and membership of the CERN Pension Fund.

• A relocation package (installation grant, removal, travel expenses) depending on your individual circumstances.

• Possibility to extend your contract up to 8 years + eligibility for indefinite contract tenure.
Overview of CERN - Discover a world where the impossible is made possible!
At CERN, the European Organization for Nuclear Research, we are pushing the frontiers of science and technology. Our groundbreaking work brings together not only physicists but also a diverse range of professionals from engineering, technical, scientific, and administrative fields. Together, we foster an environment where innovation and collaboration thrive.
Every day, we face exciting new challenges and opportunities to contribute to cutting-edge research that shapes our understanding of the universe. We meet these challenges through the diverse perspectives within our teams, ensuring every contribution is valued and driving our shared sense of inclusion and purpose. Diversity is a core value of CERN since its foundation, and it remains central to our mission and continued success.
If you are ready to be part of a dynamic, inclusive community pushing the boundaries of knowledge, CERN is the place where your curiosity and skills can thrive. Be part of our mission to uncover what lies at the heart of the universe! TAKE PART!

jobs.description:
The Worldwide LHC Computing Grid (WLCG) project is a global collaboration of around 170 computing centres in more than 40 countries, linking up national and international grid infrastructures. As computing evolves for the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) era, WLCG faces a rapidly growing computing demand alongside increasingly heterogeneous hardware environments (CPUs, GPUs, Cloud, and HPC).
 To guide procurement, resource pledging, performance studies and accounting, the High Energy Physics (HEP) community relies on domain-specific benchmarking tools to accurately measure and compare computing resources.
 As a Graduate / Applied Engineer (QUEST), you will join our team in CERN's IT Department to support the development, operation, and user support for WLCG HEPScore benchmarking services. You will contribute to key activities, helping to build and maintain the next-generation benchmarking software stack for the WLCG community.
 Your responsibilities

• Software Development: Actively contribute to the development, packaging, and distribution of the HEP benchmark software stack. Integrate, profile, and validate production-level GPU application workloads from LHC experiment software (e.g., event generation, simulation, fast inference, and HLT).

• Containerisation: Build, test, and maintain container images of HEP workloads using automated GitLab CI/CD pipelines.

• Service Maintenance & Enhancement: Ensure the smooth operation of the core benchmarking infrastructure and data ingestion services using Puppet, GitLab CI/CD, ActiveMQ, Logstash, OpenSearch, Kibana, Apache Spark and Grafana.

• Performance Analysis: Collect, process, and analyze grid-wide benchmark data to evaluate performance scaling across diverse CPU/GPU architectures and server configurations.

• Technical Support: Provide technical support and documentation to the WLCG user community.
 Your profile

• Advanced Python Development: Solid experience in Python programming,including modular code structure,packaging, distribution, and testing.

• Containerisation: Solid understanding of Docker and Apptainer/Singularity, along with familiarity with GPU container execution runtime environments.

• DevOps & Infrastructure Automation: Proficiency with GitLab CI/CD pipelines, container registries, configuration management (Puppet), and deployment methodologies.

• Linux Systems & Performance Profiling: Strong Linux administration and shell scripting skills. Experience in system metrics tracking (e.g., CPU/GPU utilisation, hardware performance metrics, power monitoring).

• Data Analytics Pipelines & Visualisation: Experience with monitoring and data analytics stacks such as OpenSearch/Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana, Grafana, or Apache Spark.

• Communication & Collaboration: Good technical writing and communication skills to interact with domain experts across the global WLCG collaboration.
 Skills

• Programming & Scripting: Python (code, packaging, testing), Bash, Git.

• Containerisation: Docker, Apptainer/Singularity.

• GPU Computing: NVIDIA Container Toolkit, CUDA, nvidia-smi, AMD ROCm, rocm-smi, GPU profiling.

• DevOps: GitLab CI/CD, Puppet, Linux administration.

• Monitoring & Data Analytics: OpenSearch/Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana, Grafana, Apache Spark, ActiveMQ.

• Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
 Eligibility criteria:

• You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State .

• You have a professional background in Applied Physics, Software Engineering (or a related field) and have either:
• a Master's degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience;

• or a PhD with no more than 3 years of post-graduation professional experience.

• You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

Job closing date: 17.11.2026 at 23:59 CET.
 Contract duration: 24 months, with a possible extension up to 36 months maximum.
 Working hours: 40 hours per week
 Job flexibility: Fully Onsite
 Target start date: 01-January-2027
 This position involves:

• Stand-by duty, when required by the needs of the Organization.

• Work during nights, Sundays and official holidays, when required by the needs of the Organization.
 Job reference: IT-CE-LCG-2026-168-GRAP
 Field of work: Information Technologies
 Benchmark job: 200020 - Computing Engineer

Global Benefits

• A monthly net stipend of either 6372 or 7004 Swiss Francs per month depending on your degree.

È particolarmente adatto a persone con un interesse per lo sviluppo FPGA o HDL, elettronica ad alta velocità, software incorporato, elaborazione digitale del segnale, strumentazione o fisica sperimentale.

• Sviluppare, integrare e testare FPGA gateware e firmware SoC incorporato per un dispositivo SoC.

• Implementare l'acquisizione dei dati e la logica del trattamento dei dati e algoritmi di elaborazione del segnale digitale in tempo reale.

• Convalida le prestazioni del sistema in ambienti di laboratorio e acceleratore.

• Eseguire l'analisi dei dati in Python.

• Assistere campagne di misura nel complesso acceleratore.

• Collabora con esperti ingegneri, fisici e tecnici di diverse squadre del CERN.

• Esperienza nell'elaborazione digitale dei segnali.

• Esperienza dimostrata con FPGA e SoC.

• Esperienza nella programmazione software (ad esempio Python, C++).

• Conoscenza di Verilog e SystemVerilog.

• Conoscenza dell'elettronica digitale.

• Conoscenza di Python.

• Parlato e scritto inglese, con un impegno per imparare il francese.

• Sei un cittadino di uno Stato membro del CERN o di uno Stato membro associato .

• un Master con 2 a 6 anni di esperienza professionale post-graduazione;

• o un dottorato con non più di 3 anni di esperienza professionale post-graduazione.

• Non hai mai avuto un contratto di laurea o di socio del CERN.

Al CERN, l'Organizzazione europea per la ricerca nucleare, stiamo spingendo le frontiere della scienza e della tecnologia. Insieme, promuoviamo un ambiente in cui l'innovazione e la collaborazione prosperano.

descriptionByLocale.de:
Die SY-BI-Gruppe in der Abteilung für Beschleunigersysteme des CERN entwickelt und betreibt die Instrumente zur Beobachtung von Teilchenstrahlen und zur Messung ihrer wichtigsten Eigenschaften. Diese Systeme sind für den zuverlässigen Betrieb, die Optimierung und die zukünftige Entwicklung des CERN-Beschleunigerkomplexes unerlässlich.
Sie werden zur Entwicklung von Strahlpositionsüberwachungssystemen der nächsten Generation für den Injektorkomplex des CERN beitragen, einschließlich der Vorbeschleuniger und des Antimaterie-Dezerlerators. Sie arbeiten an innovativen High-Speed-Datenerfassungsplattformen, die schnelle Digitalisierer mit fortschrittlichen System-on-Chip (SoC)-Technologien kombinieren.
Diese Rolle bietet eine praktische Möglichkeit, an der Schnittstelle von digitaler Elektronik, eingebetteten Systemen, Echtzeit-Signalverarbeitung und Beschleunigerphysik zu arbeiten. Es eignet sich besonders für Personen mit Interesse an FPGA- oder HDL-Entwicklung, Hochgeschwindigkeitselektronik, eingebetteter Software, digitaler Signalverarbeitung, Instrumentierung oder experimenteller Physik.
Ihre Aufgaben:

• Entwickeln, integrieren und testen Sie FPGA-Gateware und Embedded-SoC-Firmware für ein SoC-Gerät.

• Implementieren Sie Datenerfassungs- und Datenverarbeitungslogik und digitale Echtzeit-Signalverarbeitungsalgorithmen.

• Validierung der Systemleistung in Labor- und Beschleunigerumgebungen.

• Führen Sie Datenanalysen in Python durch.

• Unterstützung bei Messkampagnen im Beschleunigerkomplex.

• Arbeiten Sie mit erfahrenen Ingenieuren, Physikern und Technikern aus verschiedenen Teams des CERN zusammen.
Ihr Profil:

• Erfahrung in der digitalen Signalverarbeitung.

• Demonstrierte Erfahrung mit FPGA und SoC.

• Erfahrung in der Software-Programmierung (z.B. Python, C++).

• Nachgewiesene Erfahrungen mit Xilinx Zynq UltraScale + MPSoC und / oder RFSoC wären von Vorteil.
Fähigkeiten:

• Kenntnisse von Verilog und SystemVerilog.

• Kenntnisse der digitalen Elektronik.

• Wissen über Python.

• Englisch gesprochen und geschrieben, mit der Verpflichtung, Französisch zu lernen.
Förderkriterien:

• Sie sind Staatsangehöriger eines CERN-Mitglieds oder assoziierten Mitgliedstaats.

• Sie haben einen beruflichen Hintergrund in Elektrotechnik (oder einem verwandten Bereich) und haben entweder:
• einen Master-Abschluss mit 2 bis 6 Jahren Berufserfahrung nach dem Abschluss;

• oder einen Doktortitel mit nicht mehr als 3 Jahren Berufserfahrung nach dem Abschluss.

• Sie hatten noch nie einen CERN-Stipendiaten- oder Absolventenvertrag.

jobs.description:
You will support the Future Circular Collider ( FCC ) site investigations campaign (approximately 100 deep boreholes) - including the project management, permitting and stakeholder engagement - and the design studies for the project's underground and surface civil engineering infrastructure, as a graduate engineer with experience in geotechnical and/or underground civil engineering, joining the civil engineering team working on the FCC at CERN.
 Your responsibilities:

• Support site investigations project manager with both site-based and office support for all execution of the planning, execution and reporting of the site investigations campaign.

• Assist with design reviews of tunnels, shafts, caverns and surface structures, checking consultant deliverables against the brief, design codes and CERN requirements.

• Support geotechnical calculations and analyses.

• Help assess construction methods, including TBM and conventional excavation, and their interaction with ground conditions.

• Contribute to the project geotechnical and hydrogeological risk register and to options studies for alignment and site layout.

• Support cost estimates, construction schedules and quantity take-offs for the civil works.

• Help translate site investigation findings into design parameters and geotechnical baseline information.

• Prepare technical notes, drawings mark-ups and presentation material for internal reviews, committees and public engagement.

• Liaise with other CERN groups (integration, survey, cooling and ventilation, safety, etc.) on interfaces with the civil works.
 Your profile:

• Strong academic background in geotechnical engineering.

• First experience working in a consultancy/contractor specialising in geotechnical works, either surface or underground.

• Strong fundamentals in soil and rock mechanics.

• Basic experience of geotechnical modelling.

• Familiarity with GIS and geotechnical data management.
 Skills:

• Ability to work in an international team and adapt readily to changing requirements.

• Willingness to work on a variety of tasks as the team requires.

• Organised, able to manage several tasks and deadlines at once.

• A clear communicator, in writing and in person, with specialists and non-specialists alike.

jobs.title: Electrical Engineer for Einstein Telescope (EN-EL-EPM-2026-170-GRAP)
jobs.description:
The Electrical Group of the Engineering Department ( EN-EL ) is responsible of operation, maintenance and works on the CERN electrical network. Within the Electrical Group, you will join the Electrical Project Management Section (EPM), which is responsible for the management of projects related to the CERN's electrical transmission and distribution network and to the powering of future scientific infrastructures.
 The Einstein Telescope ( ET ) is a proposed underground facility for a third-generation gravitational-wave observatory. Building on the success of Advanced Virgo and Advanced LIGO, which detected merging black holes and neutron stars, ET will have a much higher sensitivity. This will be achieved with 10km interferometer arms (up from Virgo's 3km), a depth of 150-300 meters underground, and new technologies like cryogenic cooling of optics around 15K, quantum techniques to reduce light fluctuations, and advanced noise-reduction systems. ET will enable exploration of the Universe's gravitational waves back to the cosmological dark ages, offering insights into fundamental physics and cosmology.
 The ET project is in the 'study' phase at present and will transition into an execution project after its approval.
 Your responsibilities
 As an Electrical Engineer, you will support the mission of the group EN-EL, taking part in the studies of the electrical network and infrastructure of Einstein Telescope.
 Your main tasks will include:

• Defining the electrical requirements with users and producing the Electrical Load List.

• Preparation of conceptual design specifications and reports.

• Develop and use models of the HV, MV and LV networks of the telescope using commercially available software applications to perform various electrical system studies such as load flow, short circuit, transient stability, harmonic analysis etc.

• Preparing the transmission and distribution single line diagrams, failure mode scenarios and backup power supply solutions for both surface and underground facilities.

• Contribute to the study for a potential deployment of energy storage, grid control, FACTS, and DC grids.
 Additional tasks will include:

• Providing the inputs required and supporting the grid connection preparation.

• Perform surveys/ carry out measurements on CERN existing electrical systems (surface and underground) and other similar telescope installations globally as appropriate, to retrieve the information useful for the studies.

• Support the preparation of bill of quantities and cost estimate (CAPEX and OPEX).

• Define and review the requirements of the electrical systems and co-ordinate with the other Study team members for 3D modelling of the electrical infrastructure for its integration into the overall model and the civil works.

• Contribute to the (technological) survey of new technologies in the electrical distribution domain that could be deployed on the project.
 More information here .
 Your profile

• Experience in developing and the use of the models for High Voltage, Medium Voltage, and Low Voltage networks.

• Experience in the conceptual design of the electrical installations in the industrial facilities.

• Previous professional experience in the domain of the electrical network studies is considered an asset.

• Experience in the cost estimation processing would be an advantage.
 Skills

• Know-how/ appreciation of the Clean Room application would be an advantage.

• Knowledge of designing the underground installations would be considered as an asset.

• Innovative problem-solving attitude.

• Mindset to manoeuvre through and carry out multiple design iterations to support the early-stage development of the project.

• Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
 Eligibility criteria:

• You have a professional background in Electrical Engineering (or a related field) and have either:
• a Master's degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience;

Il Gruppo Elettrico del Dipartimento di Ingegneria (EN-EL ) è responsabile del funzionamento, della manutenzione e del funzionamento della rete elettrica CERN. All'interno del Gruppo Elettrico, si unirà alla Sezione Gestione Progetti Elettrici (EPM), che è responsabile della gestione di progetti relativi alla rete elettrica di trasmissione e distribuzione del CERN e alla potenza di future infrastrutture scientifiche.
Il Telescopio Einstein (ET ) è una struttura sotterranea proposta per un osservatorio gravitazionale di terza generazione. Basandosi sul successo di Advanced Virgo e Advanced LIGO, che ha rilevato la fusione di buchi neri e stelle di neutroni, ET avrà una sensibilità molto più alta. Questo sarà realizzato con braccio interferometro da 10km (fino a 3km di Virgo), profondità di 150-300 metri di metropolitana, e nuove tecnologie come il raffreddamento criogenico di ottiche intorno 15K, tecniche quantistiche per ridurre le fluttuazioni di luce, e sistemi di riduzione del rumore avanzati. L'ET consentirà l'esplorazione delle onde gravitazionali dell'Universo fino alle epoche oscure cosmologiche, offrendo intuizioni sulla fisica e sulla cosmologia fondamentali.
Il progetto ET è attualmente in fase 'studio' e si trasformerà in un progetto di esecuzione dopo la sua approvazione.
Le tue responsabilità
In qualità di ingegnere elettrico, supporterete la missione del gruppo EN-EL, partecipando agli studi della rete elettrica e dell'infrastruttura del telescopio Einstein.
I compiti principali includono:

• Definire i requisiti elettrici con gli utenti e produrre la Lista Carica elettrica.

• Preparazione di specifiche e report di progettazione concettuale.

• Sviluppare e utilizzare modelli delle reti HV, MV e LV del telescopio utilizzando applicazioni software commercialmente disponibili per eseguire vari studi di sistema elettrico come flusso di carico, corto circuito, stabilità transitoria, analisi armonica ecc.

Ulteriori compiti includono:

• Fornire gli ingressi necessari e sostenere la preparazione della connessione della griglia.

• Eseguire sondaggi/ effettuare misurazioni sui sistemi elettrici esistenti CERN (superficie e sotterraneo) e altre installazioni telescopiche simili a livello globale, per recuperare le informazioni utili per gli studi.

• Sostenere la preparazione della fattura di quantità e stima dei costi (CAPEX e OPEX).

• Definire e rivedere i requisiti dei sistemi elettrici e coordinare con gli altri membri del team di studio per la modellazione 3D dell'infrastruttura elettrica per la sua integrazione nel modello generale e nelle opere civili.

• Contribuire al sondaggio (tecnologico) delle nuove tecnologie nel dominio della distribuzione elettrica che potrebbe essere distribuito sul progetto.

The Electrical Group of the Engineering Department ( EN-EL ) is responsible of operation, maintenance and works on the CERN electrical network. Within the Electrical Group, you will join the Electrical Project Management Section (EPM), which is responsible for the management of projects related to the CERN's electrical transmission and distribution network and to the powering of future scientific infrastructures.
The Einstein Telescope ( ET ) is a proposed underground facility for a third-generation gravitational-wave observatory. Building on the success of Advanced Virgo and Advanced LIGO, which detected merging black holes and neutron stars, ET will have a much higher sensitivity. This will be achieved with 10km interferometer arms (up from Virgo's 3km), a depth of 150-300 meters underground, and new technologies like cryogenic cooling of optics around 15K, quantum techniques to reduce light fluctuations, and advanced noise-reduction systems. ET will enable exploration of the Universe's gravitational waves back to the cosmological dark ages, offering insights into fundamental physics and cosmology.
The ET project is in the 'study' phase at present and will transition into an execution project after its approval.
Your responsibilities
As an Electrical Engineer, you will support the mission of the group EN-EL, taking part in the studies of the electrical network and infrastructure of Einstein Telescope.
Your main tasks will include:

• Defining the electrical requirements with users and producing the Electrical Load List.

• Preparation of conceptual design specifications and reports.

• Develop and use models of the HV, MV and LV networks of the telescope using commercially available software applications to perform various electrical system studies such as load flow, short circuit, transient stability, harmonic analysis etc.

• Preparing the transmission and distribution single line diagrams, failure mode scenarios and backup power supply solutions for both surface and underground facilities.

• Contribute to the study for a potential deployment of energy storage, grid control, FACTS, and DC grids.
Additional tasks will include:

• Providing the inputs required and supporting the grid connection preparation.

• Perform surveys/ carry out measurements on CERN existing electrical systems (surface and underground) and other similar telescope installations globally as appropriate, to retrieve the information useful for the studies.

• Support the preparation of bill of quantities and cost estimate (CAPEX and OPEX).

• Define and review the requirements of the electrical systems and co-ordinate with the other Study team members for 3D modelling of the electrical infrastructure for its integration into the overall model and the civil works.

• Contribute to the (technological) survey of new technologies in the electrical distribution domain that could be deployed on the project.
More information here .
Your profile

• Experience in developing and the use of the models for High Voltage, Medium Voltage, and Low Voltage networks.

• Experience in the conceptual design of the electrical installations in the industrial facilities.

• Previous professional experience in the domain of the electrical network studies is considered an asset.

• Experience in the cost estimation processing would be an advantage.
Skills

• Know-how/ appreciation of the Clean Room application would be an advantage.

• Knowledge of designing the underground installations would be considered as an asset.

• Innovative problem-solving attitude.

• Mindset to manoeuvre through and carry out multiple design iterations to support the early-stage development of the project.

• Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
Eligibility criteria:

• You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State .

• You have a professional background in Electrical Engineering (or a related field) and have either:
• a Master's degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience;
